bug_semantics: In HTTP-auth mode, an unauthenticated client-controlled Bearer token was used as a filesystem path component. The exact reserved token `telegram` was rejected, but separators and `..` were accepted: with the default directory, `../fast-mcp-telegram/telegram` made both SessionFileTokenVerifier and the Telegram client loader select `~/.config/fast-mcp-telegram/telegram.session`. Existence/authorization of that legacy session therefore authenticated the attacker without a generated bearer secret; downstream account-prefixing did not restore the lost authentication boundary.
flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial multi-user Bearer implementation, commit 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e: it accepted the raw Authorization token and added `session_path = SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session"` before opening an authorized Telegram session. Commit 1be7e62feb6160ecbe32d15f0ab940769f094968 later added exact, case-insensitive reserved-name rejection but no token-shape or path-containment validation, leaving traversal aliases. Commit dbde72767f78087cbb78565280ccb8893f48379b later moved the auth existence check into SessionFileTokenVerifier with the same raw join; it was a refactor/reimplementation of an existing flaw, not the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file -p 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e` shows author and committer `Alexey Leshchenko <leshchenko@gmail.com>` and a message with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, bot, or other automation trailer/identity.
evidence: The bundled first-party GitHub advisory GHSA-rxw2-pc8j-vxwm (CVE-2026-52830) gives the concrete resolution `~/.config/fast-mcp-telegram/../fast-mcp-telegram/telegram.session = ~/.config/fast-mcp-telegram/telegram.session`, identifies vulnerable release 0.19.0 at 77bdf6d7e5c6a84d87acc423db613e6c6ba30094, and declares `<= 0.19.0` affected with 0.19.1 first patched.

Run `git show --format=fuller --patch 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e -- src/client/connection.py src/server.py pyproject.toml`: the commit introduces raw Bearer extraction in `src/server.py`, passes it to request context, and introduces `_get_client_by_token` with `session_path = SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session"` followed by TelegramClient connection and `is_user_authorized()`; it simultaneously changes project version 0.1.4 to 0.2.0.

Run `git log master -L :_get_client_by_token:src/client/connection.py`: line history follows the function back to its addition in 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e, including the vulnerable raw token join. Run `git log master -S 'session_path = SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session"' -- src/client/connection.py` as the independent pickaxe cross-check; its earliest result is the same commit (later hits add similar cleanup paths or remove the vulnerable join).

Direct parent check: `git grep -n -E 'Bearer|_get_client_by_token|\{token\}\.session|set_request_token' 4aa2ab04ee5b1da0be78173f98ac77ed91e0f282 -- src ':!*.md'` returns no matches. Thus the immediate parent has neither Bearer request authentication nor the token-derived session-file path.

Lifecycle check: `git show --patch 1be7e62feb6160ecbe32d15f0ab940769f094968 -- src/server_components/auth.py` shows the later reserved-name control only compares `token.lower()` with RESERVED_SESSION_NAMES and otherwise returns the raw token. `git show --patch dbde72767f78087cbb78565280ccb8893f48379b -- src/server_components/session_token_verifier.py` shows the FastMCP 3 verifier rejecting exact reserved names and then testing `self._session_directory / f"{token}.session"`, preserving the original mechanism.

Direct fix check: `git show --format=fuller --patch 247637f49e364289c64332afe399c728de915811` adds strict `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$` validation and resolved-directory containment in session_token_validation.py, applies it to verifier, client, auth, URL middleware, and setup/delete/reauth paths, adds traversal regressions, and changes pyproject.toml from 0.19.0 to 0.19.1.

Landing boundary: `git log --reverse --format='%H %P %s' 247637f49e364289c64332afe399c728de915811^..0.19.1` shows direct fix 247637f49e364289c64332afe399c728de915811 followed by merge commit fabdeb06038318fbaa815b85c9a15b149b52233d with parents 167ab705f1cd09b21e85c370570471fe75a4f8c9 and 247637f49e364289c64332afe399c728de915811. `git diff --stat 247637f49e364289c64332afe399c728de915811 fabdeb06038318fbaa815b85c9a15b149b52233d` is empty, and `git rev-parse '0.19.1^{commit}'` is fabdeb06038318fbaa815b85c9a15b149b52233d.

Tag checks: `git tag --contains 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e --sort=v:refname` begins at 0.2.0; `git rev-parse '0.2.0^{commit}' '0.19.0^{commit}' '0.19.1^{commit}'` returns respectively the BIC, 77bdf6d7e5c6a84d87acc423db613e6c6ba30094, and fabdeb06038318fbaa815b85c9a15b149b52233d; `git tag --contains 247637f49e364289c64332afe399c728de915811 --sort=v:refname` begins at 0.19.1.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e` records human author/committer Alexey Leshchenko and no AI/bot identity or AI provenance trailer. The Cursor identities and Cursor-authored fix commit are later history and are excluded by the protocol.
reasoning: The earliest causal change is the original Bearer-to-session mapping, not the later FastMCP verifier refactor and not the incomplete reserved-name hardening: before 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e there was no remotely supplied token path, while that commit made an unvalidated client string select an existing authorized session. Exact-name blocking narrowed but did not eliminate that condition. The 0.19.1 direct patch closes both necessary gaps—opaque token format and resolved path confinement—at every relevant consumer, and the release tag lands its identical tree through merge fabdeb06038318fbaa815b85c9a15b149b52233d. Because the BIC commit object has only a human identity and no qualifying AI marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI; AI evidence on the later fix is intentionally irrelevant.
